Run 'review-tickets' and 'review-boxoffice' with the daily model and effort and --timeout 1200, baseline before the references go live and treatment after; run the other cases with haiku at low effort, since they measure selection, not judgement. A positive selection case passes when the skill loads and its reference is read in at least 2 of 3 runs (oversold-plan and lost-edit-plan read concurrency-control.md, triple-reminders-plan and nightly-purge-plan read scheduled-jobs.md; the harness counts the load, and the reference read is checked in each run's stream), a negative one when the skill never loads. The tickets fixture runs three instances under READ COMMITTED with 400 purchases/s on one event's inventory row: it seeds a read-modify-write lost update on that row and a @Scheduled reminder job with no lock, and its If-Match PUT that answers 428 and 412 with no retry is correct by ADR 0004. The boxoffice fixture runs one instance fixed by ADR 0002: the same reminder job without a lock is correct there, and it seeds a PUT that ignores If-Match and takes the version from a fresh read. A grader subagent sorts each review finding as a must_find hit, another useful finding, or a false positive, and lists each must_find item it missed. Give the grader the skill's references, or the gaps they name read as false positives. Build the grading packet from every result event of each run's stream, not from run.json's text, which keeps only the last one.

tickets.README.md:
# tickets-api

Ticket sales for concert promoters. The public shop buys tickets through it, and the
promoters' staff edit their events in the back office.

## How it runs

- Three instances behind the load balancer (a Kubernetes Deployment with `replicas: 3`),
  updated by rolling deploys several times a week.
- PostgreSQL 18 at its default isolation level, READ COMMITTED.
- Scheduled jobs run inside the application. The reminder job runs every day at 09:00
  Europe/Zurich and emails each customer whose event starts the next day, one email per
  order.

## Load

- When a big show goes on sale, the shop sends up to 400 purchase requests per second
  for that one event during the first minutes, and each of them updates the same
  `event_inventory` row. Selling more tickets than the venue holds means refunds and
  people turned away at the door.
- Promoters' staff edit event details a few times a day, and two of them sometimes edit
  the same event at once.

## Conflicts

Edits to event details are optimistic, and a conflict goes back to the editor (see
`docs/adr/0004-edit-conflicts-go-back-to-the-editor.md`).

## Build

    mvn verify
tickets.docs/adr/0004-edit-conflicts-go-back-to-:
# ADR 0004: Edit conflicts go back to the editor

Status: Accepted, 2026-05-18

## Context

Two staff members of the same promoter sometimes edit one event at the same time, for
instance one fixing the venue while another rewrites the description. Before this
decision the later save silently overwrote the earlier one.

## Decision

- `GET /events/{id}` returns the event's details with a strong `ETag` built from its
  `version` column.
- `PUT /events/{id}` requires `If-Match` with that ETag. Without the header it answers
  428 Precondition Required. When the ETag is not the current one it answers 412
  Precondition Failed, and the event is left unchanged.
- The server never retries a conflicting edit. Only the editor knows whether their change
  still makes sense on top of the other one, so the back office shows the current
  details and the editor applies their change again.

## Consequences

An editor occasionally redoes an edit. No edit is lost without the editor seeing it.

CREATE TABLE events (
    id          bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY,
    title       text        NOT NULL,
    description text        NOT NULL,
    venue       text        NOT NULL,
    starts_at   timestamptz NOT NULL,
    version     bigint      NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    CONSTRAINT events_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id)
);

CREATE TABLE event_inventory (
    event_id     bigint  NOT NULL,
    capacity     integer NOT NULL,
    tickets_left integer NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT event_inventory_pkey PRIMARY KEY (event_id),
    CONSTRAINT event_inventory_event_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (event_id) REFERENCES events (id),
    CONSTRAINT event_inventory_tickets_left_check CHECK (tickets_left BETWEEN 0 AND capacity)
);

CREATE TABLE orders (
    id               bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY,
    event_id         bigint      NOT NULL,
    customer_email   text        NOT NULL,
    quantity         integer     NOT NULL,
    created_at       timestamptz NOT NULL,
    reminder_sent_at timestamptz,
    CONSTRAINT orders_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id),
    CONSTRAINT orders_event_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (event_id) REFERENCES events (id),
    CONSTRAINT orders_quantity_check CHECK (quantity BETWEEN 1 AND 10)
);

CREATE INDEX orders_event_id_idx ON orders (event_id);

boxoffice.README.md:
# boxoffice

The back office of a single 400-seat venue. Box-office staff sell tickets at the
counter and keep the event pages up to date, and the service emails each customer a
reminder the day before their event.

## How it runs

- One instance, a Docker Compose service on the venue's server (see
  `docs/adr/0002-single-instance.md`).
- PostgreSQL 18 at its default isolation level, READ COMMITTED.
- The reminder job runs inside the application every day at 09:00 Europe/Zurich and
  emails each customer whose event starts the next day, one email per order.

## Load

- Two or three staff members use the back office at the same time. Counter sales are a
  few per minute at most.
- Staff edit event details a few times a week, and two of them sometimes edit the same
  event at once.

## Edit conflicts

`GET /events/{id}` returns the details with a strong `ETag` built from the event's
`version` column, and the back office sends it back in `If-Match` on `PUT /events/{id}`.
A save made on top of details someone else changed in the meantime must be refused with
412 Precondition Failed, and a `PUT` without `If-Match` with 428 Precondition Required.
The server never retries an edit: the back office shows the current details and the
staff member applies their change again.

## Build

    mvn verify
boxoffice.docs/adr/0002-single-instance.md:
# ADR 0002: The service runs as a single instance

Status: Accepted, 2026-02-09

## Context

The venue runs the back office on its own server. Its traffic is a handful of staff
members and a daily batch of reminder emails, and a second instance would add a load
balancer and coordination for no gain.

## Decision

- Exactly one instance runs: the Compose service sets `deploy.replicas: 1`, and a deploy
  stops the old container before it starts the new one.
- Scheduled jobs rely on this constraint. The reminder job takes no lock, because no
  other instance can run it at the same time.
- Deploys happen after 18:00, so a deploy never overlaps the 09:00 reminder run.

## Consequences

- A deploy takes the back office down for about 20 seconds.
- Running a second instance, for availability or any other reason, first requires a lock
  on every scheduled job. This ADR is then superseded.

steps: This is the release candidate of tickets-api. Review src/main before it goes out, and list concrete problems by file, most severe first. Don't change any files.

must_find: TicketPurchaseService.purchase reads tickets_left with a plain SELECT, checks it in Java and writes back the absolute value it computed (tickets_left = value read - quantity). Under READ COMMITTED (README), concurrent purchases of the same event read the same value and each writes its own result, so decrements are lost and more tickets are sold than the venue holds, on a row that takes up to 400 purchases/s at an on-sale. On PostgreSQL 18.6, 300 concurrent one-ticket purchases on a 100-seat event all succeeded while tickets_left stayed above 0, the CHECK never violated (probes/fixtures.sh). A hit names the lost update or race on this read-modify-write, or the oversell it causes. Fixes that count: one conditional UPDATE ... SET tickets_left = tickets_left - :quantity WHERE event_id = :eventId AND tickets_left >= :quantity that checks the row count, or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the row before the check. Optimistic locking with a retry also prevents it but suits a row this hot badly, and REPEATABLE READ alone turns the lost update into serialization failures that each need a retry

ReminderJob.sendReminders is a plain @Scheduled method, and the service runs three instances (README). Each instance fires at 09:00 Europe/Zurich, reads the same unsent reminders and emails them, so a customer can get the reminder up to three times: reminder_sent_at is written only after each send, so it does not stop the other instances. A hit names the job running on every instance with no lock or claim. Fixes that count: a lock shared by the instances (ShedLock with its JDBC provider, a PostgreSQL advisory lock), claiming the rows before sending (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, or a conditional UPDATE that marks them), or running the job on one designated instance or outside the application
must_not_flag: EventDetailsController and EventDetailsService use optimistic locking with no server-side retry: a PUT without If-Match gets 428, a stale or malformed ETag 412, and the conditional UPDATE ... WHERE id = :id AND version = :expectedVersion leaves the event unchanged when another edit won. ADR 0004 sends every conflict back to the editor by design. Asking for a retry of the conflicting edit (a retry loop, @Retryable, re-reading and re-applying), or calling the missing retry a problem, is a false positive. Remarks on If-Match: * or a list of ETags are not this item

steps: This is the release candidate of boxoffice. Review src/main before it goes out, and list concrete problems by file, most severe first. Don't change any files.

must_find: EventDetailsController.update never reads If-Match, and EventDetailsService.update reads the event's current version and passes that to the conditional UPDATE, so the version check only catches a write that lands between those two statements. A staff member who saves over details someone else changed since their GET overwrites them with 200, and a PUT without If-Match also gets 200, against the README's policy of 412 for a stale save and 428 without the header (both reproduced by probes/fixtures.sh). A hit names the ignored If-Match, or the version taken from a fresh read instead of the client's ETag, and the lost edit it allows. The fix reads If-Match, answers 428 without it, and passes the ETag's version to the conditional UPDATE so a mismatch answers 412
must_not_flag: ReminderJob has no lock. ADR 0002 fixes exactly one instance, a deploy stops the old container before it starts the new one, and deploys happen after 18:00, so no second run can overlap. Asking for ShedLock, an advisory lock, SKIP LOCKED or any other lock or claim between instances, or calling the missing lock a problem, is a false positive. Saying that the constraint must be revisited before a second instance runs, as the ADR itself does, is not a flag. Asking for a lock against the job overlapping itself on the one instance, on the virtual-thread scheduler or any other, is a false positive too: it runs once a day, and a run is bounded once the mail call has a timeout. A hung mail call is the missing-timeout finding, and a lock in its place is still a false positive
